description: A single looper track, either on its own or as an expander adding a track to sickoLooper1; it goes immediately to the right of that module or of another expander

params.text: Sets the level of the stereo input, 0 to 200%, with the centre at 100%
Silences the input; it has to be off before anything can be recorded
Sets how many bars the loop lasts, 1 to 16
Ties the track to the master module's clock, so a command takes effect on the next bar; standing alone this module always records and plays unsynced whatever this button is set to
Starts an idle track at the position the bar has already reached, instead of waiting for the loop to come round
Stops a playing or overdubbing track at once with an 8ms fade, instead of waiting for the loop to end
Plays, records or overdubs the loop once and then leaves the track idle
Plays or overdubs the loop backwards; the direction changes only when the loop reaches its end
Sets the crossfade between the end of a loop and its restart, 0 to 1000ms; it comes up at 8ms
Pans the track's own stereo output
Sets the level of the track's output, 0% to 100%
Starts recording on an empty track, or overdubbing on one that already holds a loop
Starts playback of the recorded loop; the PLAY Button Sequence menu item changes what repeated presses do
Double-click to erase the recorded loop; it only works while the track is idle
Sends the source signal straight to the track's own outputs as well

inputs.text: The left channel of the source to record; with nothing in the right jack this one is used for both
The right channel of the source to record
A trigger here does what the REC button does
A trigger here does what the PLAY button does
A trigger here does what the STOP button does
A trigger here erases the recorded loop
Plays the loop faster or slower, one octave per volt, which changes its pitch
A trigger here flips the loop's playback direction, as the REV button does
Moves the pan, over the range chosen under PAN CV range

outputs.text: The left channel of the track output
The right channel of the track output
A 1ms pulse when the loop reaches its end, and on a forced stop when 'EOL pulse on stop' is ticked

notes: with no sickoLooper1 to its left this module records and plays unsynced loops whatever the SYNC button says; synchronisation comes back as soon as a master is found.
nothing is recorded until the MUTE button is off and a source is connected; the level is set with the LVL knob while you test it.
there is no clock section, no tempo detection and no preset file handling here; the clock, the click and the all-tracks controls come from the sickoLooper1 to the left.
the PLAY and REC lights show the state: both off is empty, PLAY lit steady is idle, PLAY flashing is playing, REC flashing is recording, both flashing is overdubbing.
a fast flash on PLAY or REC means a command has been given and takes effect at the end of the loop; pressing the same button again cancels it.
right-clicking the track's bar display opens the track menu: Fade IN on playback, Play Full Tail on Stop, Import Wav, Export Wav, Extra samples Tail (1sec).
menu: PLAY Button Sequence — sets what the PLAY button and its jack do: start and stop, or record then play then overdub, or record then overdub then play, with STOP the only way out of the last two
Instant STOP button — makes the STOP button drop the track to idle at once, except during the first recording of a synced track
OVERDUB after REC — moves the track into overdub by itself at the end of its first recording
EOL pulse on stop — sends a pulse from the EoL output when the loop is forced to stop as well as at its natural end
PAN CV range: 0/10v, ± 5v, ±10v — sets the voltage span the PAN CV jack covers
Track settings — opens the same items the track's bar display carries, from the module's own menu
Add Expander — places another sickoLooperX to the right, chained to the same master
